add_reaction_step.description: Appends a compatible reaction step to a synthesis or transformation chain.

valid_transformations.conditions: hν (UV/visible light); gas phase or CCl₄ solvent; room temperature. Radical chain: initiation X₂+hν→2X•; propagation X•+R-H→HX+R•, R•+X₂→RX+X•; termination by radical coupling. Cl₂ less selective than Br₂ (ΔH‡ earlier, less selective TS). All C-H bonds compete; tertiary>secondary>primary selectivity. Br₂ selectivity: 3°:2°:1° ≈ 1600:82:1.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; 1–3 atm H₂; heterogeneous Pd/C, Pt, Ni or Raney-Ni catalyst. Syn addition: both H atoms delivered to same face from catalyst surface. Ethanol or ethyl acetate solvent typical. Degree of substitution slows rate (more hindered alkene → slower). Raney-Ni requires no high-pressure apparatus.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT or 0°C; polar non-protic solvent (CH₂Cl₂) or neat; ionic mechanism. Step 1: H⁺ protonates alkene at less-substituted C → more stable carbocation (Markovnikov). Step 2: X⁻ attacks carbocation (no face selectivity → racemic at new stereocentre). Reactivity order HX: HI>HBr>HCl. More substituted alkene = faster (more stable carbocation intermediate).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; non-polar or CCl₄ solvent; radical chain mechanism initiated by peroxide (ROOR) thermolysis or hν. Peroxide→RO•→adds to less-substituted C of alkene (anti-Markovnikov: avoids steric strain at radical) → secondary/tertiary radical → Br• transfer from HBr. Only HBr works (HCl and HI do NOT give anti-Markovnikov product).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; aqueous acetone or t-BuOH/H₂O solvent; catalytic OsO₄ with NMO as co-oxidant (Upjohn conditions). OsO₄ forms cyclic osmate ester intermediate (concerted [3+2]) → syn delivery of both OH groups. Stoichiometric OsO₄ alternative uses NaHSO₃ workup. For small scale: OsO₄ (cat.)/NMO/H₂O/acetone. Product: syn (cis) diol, enantiomeric mixture for achiral alkenes.
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemistry: syn-diol from OsO₄ or cold KMnO₄; anti-diol from epoxide then H₂O/base. Specify workup conditions explicitly in answers.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; aqueous H₂SO₄ or dil KMnO₄/cold; indirect anti-dihydroxylation via epoxide intermediate. Step 1: mCPBA→epoxide (retention). Step 2: H₃O⁺ or HO⁻ opens epoxide (SN2, backside → anti addition of OH groups). Cold dilute KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent) gives SYN diol (not anti); anti diol requires epoxide route.
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemistry: syn-diol from OsO₄ or cold KMnO₄; anti-diol from epoxide then H₂O/base. Specify workup conditions explicitly in answers.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; CH₂Cl₂ solvent; mCPBA (meta-chloroperoxybenzoic acid) or peracetic acid; concerted [1+2] cycloaddition (butterfly TS). Retention of alkene geometry (cis-alkene→cis-epoxide; trans-alkene→trans-epoxide). More electron-rich alkene reacts faster. Product is strained 3-membered ring (epoxide). mCPBA stored cold, handled with care (oxidising solid).
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemical outcome critical: syn addition (mCPBA), then ring-opening gives anti-addition overall. Track face selectivity carefully.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; aqueous Br₂ (Br₂/H₂O); anti addition. Step 1: Br⁺ (electrophile) attacks alkene π-bond → bridged bromonium ion intermediate. Step 2: H₂O (better nucleophile than Br⁻ in aqueous) attacks bromonium at more substituted C (anti, SN2-like) → trans-bromohydrin. Product: β-bromo alcohol with OH at more substituted C and Br at less substituted C (when H₂O is solvent).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Aqueous H₂SO₄ (dil.) or H₃O⁺; Markovnikov addition; ionic mechanism via carbocation. Step 1: H⁺ protonates alkene → more stable carbocation. Step 2: H₂O attacks → oxonium ion → deprotonation → alcohol. Gives Markovnikov product. Prone to rearrangements (1,2-hydride or 1,2-alkyl shift if more stable carbocation available). RT to 60°C.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1 (hydroboration): RT; dry THF solvent; anhydrous conditions; BH₃·THF added to alkene → boron goes to less-substituted C (anti-Markovnikov, syn addition). Step 2 (oxidation): 0°C→RT; H₂O₂ (30%), NaOH(aq); replaces B with OH with retention of configuration. Overall: syn, anti-Markovnikov addition of H₂O. No rearrangements.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: –78°C to RT; ozonolysis in CH₂Cl₂ or MeOH; O₃ (ozonator). Reductive workup: Zn/H₂O, Zn/AcOH, PPh₃, or Me₂S → aldehydes/ketones (no further oxidation). Oxidative workup: H₂O₂ → carboxylic acids from terminal alkene; H₂O₂/AcOH → carboxylic acids. Mechanism: [3+2] cycloaddition → carbonyl oxide (molozonide) → ozonide → workup.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'II'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; non-polar solvent (CCl₄ or CH₂Cl₂); anti addition. Step 1: X₂ (X=Cl,Br) polarised → X⁺ attacks alkene → bridged halonium ion. Step 2: X⁻ attacks from opposite face (SN2 anti) → trans-dihalide. cis-alkene → anti product (threo); trans-alkene → anti product (erythro). Br₂/CCl₄ reaction decolorisation is test for alkene unsaturation.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; 1 atm H₂; Lindlar's catalyst (Pd on CaCO₃, poisoned with Pb(OAc)₂ and quinoline) or Pd/BaSO₄/quinoline. Syn addition of H₂ → cis-alkene (Z-alkene). Catalyst surface delivers both H atoms from same face. Stop at 1 equivalent H₂ (mono-reduction). Quinoline/Pb²⁺ poisons reduce activity so reaction stops at alkene stage.
valid_transformations.notes: Elimination: specify Saytzeff (small base, more substituted) vs Hofmann (bulky base/Hofmann exhaustive/N-oxide, less substituted) product.

valid_transformations.conditions: –33°C; liquid NH₃ solvent (dissolving metal conditions); Na or Li metal. Mechanism: Na→e⁻(solvated); e⁻ adds to alkyne → vinyl radical anion → protonation by NH₃ → vinyl radical → 2nd e⁻ addition → vinyl anion (trans, more stable) → protonation → trans-alkene (E-alkene). Anti addition overall. More stable trans-radical → trans product.
valid_transformations.notes: Elimination: specify Saytzeff (small base, more substituted) vs Hofmann (bulky base/Hofmann exhaustive/N-oxide, less substituted) product.

valid_transformations.conditions: 333K (60°C); aqueous H₂SO₄ (dil.); HgSO₄ catalyst (mercuric sulphate as Lewis acid). Mechanism: Hg²⁺ activates alkyne → vinyl-Hg intermediate → water attacks → vinyl alcohol (enol) → keto-enol tautomerism → ketone (Markovnikov product; internal alkynes give ketones, terminal alkynes give methyl ketone). Lindlar/mild conditions not needed — acidic aqueous.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; liquid NH₃ or THF; NaNH₂ (sodamide, strong base pKa≈38). Deprotonation of terminal C-H (pKa≈25): RC≡C-H + NaNH₂ → RC≡C⁻Na⁺ + NH₃. Internal alkynes (no terminal C-H) do NOT react. Acetylide is strong nucleophile for SN2 on primary alkyl halides. Dry conditions (NH₃ solvent or THF); avoid moisture.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; aqueous NaOH or KOH (aq.); SN2 for primary/secondary R-X (inversion of configuration). Tertiary R-X undergoes E2 (elimination preferred under basic aq. conditions). Mechanism: HO⁻ attacks back-face of C-X → inversion. Solvent: H₂O or H₂O/EtOH mixture. Primary > secondary for SN2; tertiary → mostly elimination. SN2 rate: MeX > 1° > 2° >> 3°.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; alcoholic KOH (ethanolic KOH) or t-BuOK/t-BuOH; heat required; E2 mechanism. Anti-periplanar geometry required (H and X must be anti). Saytzeff product (more-substituted alkene) preferred with small bases (KOH/EtOH). Hofmann product preferred with bulky bases (t-BuOK). Tertiary > secondary > primary for E2 rate. Competition with SN2: polar aprotic → SN2; polar protic/base/heat → E2.
valid_transformations.notes: Elimination: specify Saytzeff (small base, more substituted) vs Hofmann (bulky base/Hofmann exhaustive/N-oxide, less substituted) product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Aqueous acidic conditions (Zn/HCl or Zn/H⁺); reductive dehalogenation. Zinc metal (or Mg) provides 2 electrons: R-X + Zn + H⁺ → R-H + ZnX⁺. Alternative: LiAlH₄ (dry ether, RT). For gem-dihalides: Zn/HCl removes both halogens to give alkene, then further reduction to alkane. Used in synthesis to remove halogens introduced in HVZ or halogenation steps.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Anhydrous, inert atmosphere (N₂ or Ar); dry ether (diethyl ether) or dry THF solvent; Mg metal turnings; RT or gentle warming. Must exclude moisture strictly (Grignard reacts immediately with H₂O). Mg inserts into C-X bond: R-X + Mg(0) → R-Mg-X. Reactivity order: R-I > R-Br > R-Cl >> R-F. Vinyl and aryl halides require THF (higher bp) and sometimes I₂ activation of Mg surface.
valid_transformations.notes: Strict anhydrous conditions required. Proton source (H₂O, ROH) destroys Grignard before reaction with substrate.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; DMSO or DMF solvent (polar aprotic); NaCN or KCN. SN2 mechanism: CN⁻ attacks back-face of primary/secondary C-X → R-CN (nitrile, inversion). Ambident nucleophile: C-attack (CN⁻) preferred in polar aprotic → nitrile. N-attack (isocyanide R-NC) minor product. Primary and secondary R-X only; tertiary → E2. Chain length increases by 1C. Product used for homologation.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Excess NH₃ (sealed vessel or pressure); heat; SN2. Primary alkyl halides preferred. Product mixture: R-X + NH₃ → R-NH₂ → R-NH₃⁺X⁻ (salt, then free with base). But R-NH₂ also attacks R-X → 2°, 3°, and quaternary ammonium salt. Use excess NH₃ to favour primary amine. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis gives pure primary amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to reflux; dry aprotic solvent (DMF, DMSO, or ether); SN2. Sodium/potassium alkoxide (R'ONa/R'OK) prepared first (alcohol + Na). R'O⁻ + R-X → R-O-R' + X⁻. MUST use primary R-X (secondary gives E2; tertiary gives only E2). Best: R'ONa + CH₃I or primary alkyl halide. Dry conditions (alkoxides react with H₂O).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; dry acetone solvent; NaI (sodium iodide). Equilibrium driven right because NaCl or NaBr is insoluble in acetone and precipitates. SN2 mechanism (inversion at C). Acetone must be anhydrous. Used to convert R-Cl or R-Br to R-I for subsequent reactions requiring better leaving group. Rate: primary > secondary >> tertiary.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ solvent; PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) or PDC. Mild oxidant: stops at aldehyde from primary alcohol. Does NOT oxidise to carboxylic acid. Secondary alcohol → ketone. Tertiary alcohol → no reaction. Alternative mild oxidants: Swern (oxalyl chloride/DMSO/Et₃N, –78°C), MnO₂ (allylic/benzylic only), Dess-Martin periodinane (DMP).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; anhydrous CH₂Cl₂ solvent; PCC or K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ (Jones reagent, aqueous). Secondary alcohol → ketone. PCC in CH₂Cl₂: mild, anhydrous, stops at ketone. Jones (CrO₃/H₂SO₄/acetone): secondary alcohol → ketone. Swern oxidation (–78°C): secondary → ketone. Oppenauer oxidation (Al-alkoxide/ketone, mild): secondary → ketone.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; acidic aqueous conditions; KMnO₄/H⁺ or K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ or Jones reagent. Primary alcohol → aldehyde (intermediate) → carboxylic acid (overoxidation). Aqueous conditions allow the aldehyde hydrate to form, which is then oxidised. Use Jones (CrO₃/H₂SO₄/acetone) for clean conversion. Secondary alcohol → ketone (NOT further oxidised to acid under these conditions).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; concentrated H₂SO₄ (>170°C, >443K) or Al₂O₃ (>300°C) or POCl₃/pyridine; E1 or E2 mechanism. Saytzeff product (more substituted alkene) preferred. H₂SO₄ mechanism: OH protonated → oxonium → loss of H₂O → carbocation → E1 → alkene. Order of ease: 3° > 2° > 1°. Rearrangement possible if more stable carbocation accessible via 1,2-shift.
valid_transformations.notes: Elimination: specify Saytzeff (small base, more substituted) vs Hofmann (bulky base/Hofmann exhaustive/N-oxide, less substituted) product.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; anhydrous conditions; SOCl₂ with pyridine (→ R-Cl, SN2, inversion) or PBr₃ (→ R-Br, inversion) or HX (R-Cl, R-Br, R-I; SN1 for 3°, SN2 for 1°). SOCl₂ + pyridine: pyridine prevents SNi (retention), ensures SN2 (inversion). SOCl₂ without pyridine (SNi, retention of configuration). PCl₅: vigorous conditions, inversion. Lucas test: ZnCl₂/conc HCl — 3° (immediate turbidity), 2° (turbidity after heating), 1° (no reaction cold).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; anhydrous conditions; base (pyridine or Et₃N) to neutralise HCl generated; acyl chloride (RCOCl) + alcohol → ester + HCl. Alternatively acyl anhydride (slow, no base needed). Fischer esterification: RCOOH + R'OH, H⁺ cat., reflux, equilibrium (remove H₂O). Acyl chloride route: fast, irreversible, suitable for sterically hindered or acid-sensitive alcohols.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: Na metal (or NaH) + ROH → RONa + ½H₂; dry conditions, 0°C to RT. Step 2: RONa + R'X → ROR' (Williamson synthesis, SN2, dry aprotic solvent). Alternatively: conc H₂SO₄ at 110–140°C for symmetrical ether (inter-molecular dehydration, SN2). Tertiary alcohols → only alkene under acid (E1 preferred).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; Tollens' reagent ([Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺, alkaline) → silver mirror (RT); Fehling's (Cu²⁺/tartrate, alkaline, heat) → Cu₂O brick-red precipitate; KMnO₄/H⁺ or K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺ (acidic, RT to reflux). Benedict's: similar to Fehling's but citrate buffer (milder). Aldehydes oxidised; ketones NOT oxidised by Tollens'/Fehling's (except α-hydroxy ketones). Formic acid gives positive Tollens' (can be oxidised to CO₂).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; protic solvent (EtOH or EtOH/H₂O); NaBH₄ (sodium borohydride) — mild, safe, selective. Alternative: LiAlH₄ (dry ether, anhydrous, more powerful). NaBH₄: reduces aldehydes and ketones but NOT esters, acids, amides. LiAlH₄: reduces all C=O including esters, acids, amides. Mechanism: H⁻ delivered from B or Al to electrophilic carbonyl C → alkoxide → protonation during workup.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: Reflux in acetic acid/HCl; Zn-Hg amalgam (Clemmensen reduction). Strongly acidic conditions (conc HCl). Mechanism uncertain but involves carbenoid/zinc-carbenoid intermediate on metal surface; not via alcohol intermediate. Aldehyde or ketone directly → CH₂ (methylene). Alternative: Wolff-Kishner (NH₂NH₂/KOH/EG, reflux 200°C) — for base-sensitive substrates avoid; acid-sensitive → use Clemmensen. Both go C=O → CH₂.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to RT; buffered slightly acidic or neutral conditions (pH ~5); HCN or NaCN/H₂SO₄. Mechanism: CN⁻ (nucleophile) attacks electrophilic carbonyl C → alkoxide → protonation → cyanohydrin (α-hydroxynitrile). Equilibrium (reversible). Aldehydes > ketones (less hindered). HCN alone is slow (no CN⁻); NaCN + HCl or KCN + H₂SO₄ generates CN⁻ in situ. Chiral (racemic mixture unless asymmetric catalyst used).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; dry HCl or p-TsOH (acid catalyst); excess dry alcohol (2 equiv ROH); anhydrous conditions (remove H₂O to drive equilibrium). Mechanism: H⁺ protonates C=O → oxocarbenium → first ROH attack → hemiacetal → protonation of OH → loss of H₂O → oxocarbenium → 2nd ROH → acetal. Reverse (hydrolysis) occurs in aqueous acid. Acetals are stable to base; used as protecting groups.
valid_transformations.notes: Protecting group strategy: acetal stable to base/LiAlH₄; removed by dilute acid. Ensure the protecting group is compatible with all subsequent steps.

valid_transformations.conditions: Slightly acidic conditions (pH 4–5); aqueous or alcoholic; –H₂O (condensation, remove water or use Dean-Stark). Mechanism: amine nucleophile attacks C=O → carbinolamine (hemiaminal) → protonation of OH → loss of H₂O → iminium → deprotonation → imine. Aldehydes > ketones (less steric). 1° amine required (2° amine → enamine). Acid catalyses dehydration; too acidic protonates amine (less nucleophilic).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0–5°C; dilute NaOH (5–10% aq.); cold conditions (aldol condensation: cold=aldol addition product; hot=dehydrated enone). Mechanism: OH⁻ deprotonates α-H → enolate → attacks C=O of 2nd aldehyde → β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol). Cold conditions stop at addition; heat → dehydration → α,β-unsaturated aldehyde (aldol condensation product). Requires α-H. Mixed aldol if two different carbonyls.
valid_transformations.notes: Aldol addition (cold) vs condensation (warm): specify temperature. Crossed aldol requires careful substrate choice to avoid four-product mixture.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; protic solvent (EtOH or EtOH/H₂O); NaBH₄ (mild, selective). Alternative: LiAlH₄ (dry ether, 0°C, anhydrous). Mechanism: H⁻ from BH₄⁻ attacks electrophilic carbonyl C of ketone → alkoxide → protonation → secondary alcohol. NaBH₄: selective (aldehydes and ketones only, NOT esters). New stereocentre formed — racemic mixture (unless chiral catalyst). Facial selectivity governed by steric approach.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Wolff-Kishner: hydrazone formation first (NH₂NH₂, EtOH, RT) then base/heat (KOH, ethylene glycol, reflux 200°C). Mechanism: C=O + NH₂NH₂ → hydrazone (C=N-NH₂) → base removes N-H → anion → loss of N₂ → carbanion → protonation → CH₂. Base-sensitive substrates: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/conc HCl) instead. Bamford-Stevens: tosylhydrazone + base → diazo intermediate → carbene/alkene.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: pH 4–5 (buffered slightly acidic); aqueous-alcoholic; NH₂OH·HCl (hydroxylamine hydrochloride) + base (pyridine or NaOAc). Condensation: C=O + NH₂OH → carbinolamine → –H₂O → oxime (C=N-OH). Syn/anti isomers possible (E/Z about C=N bond). Ketones give ketoximes; aldehydes give aldoximes. Beckmann rearrangement converts oxime → amide (H₂SO₄, PCl₅, or BF₃; group anti to OH migrates).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'II'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to RT; neutral to slightly acidic; HCN or KCN/H₂SO₄. CN⁻ attacks ketone carbonyl (less reactive than aldehyde due to steric + electronic factors). Equilibrium lies to left for sterically hindered ketones. Acetone cyanohydrin → methyl methacrylate (industrial). Product: α-hydroxy nitrile (racemic).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to reflux; acid catalyst (H⁺, p-TsOH, or BF₃); excess alcohol; Dean-Stark or molecular sieves (remove H₂O). Mechanism: acid protonates ketone → oxocarbenium → alcohol attacks → β-alkoxy alcohol → loss of H₂O → enol ether. Enol ethers stable to base but hydrolysed easily by aqueous acid → ketone. Used as protecting groups for ketones.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Fischer esterification: reflux; H₂SO₄ or dry HCl catalyst; excess alcohol or remove H₂O (Dean-Stark); equilibrium. Mechanism: H⁺ protonates C=O → tetrahedral intermediate → ROH attacks → loss of H₂O → ester. Reversible; drive right by excess ROH or remove H₂O. Steric: 2,6-disubstituted (hindered) acids don't esterify well by Fischer → use DCC coupling or acyl chloride.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; neat SOCl₂ or small excess; anhydrous; mild heat if needed. SOCl₂ + RCOOH → RCOCl + SO₂ + HCl (both gases leave → irreversible). Alternative: PCl₅ (harsher), PCl₃ (milder). Oxalyl chloride (ClCOCOCl) + cat. DMF (Vilsmeier): very mild, RT for acid chloride formation. Dry conditions (acid chlorides hydrolyse readily with H₂O).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Direct: heat RCOOH + NH₃ (or amine) → ammonium salt → strong heat → amide + H₂O. High temperature required (150–200°C); loss of H₂O. Better route: acid chloride + amine (faster, milder). DCC coupling: RCOOH + amine + DCC (RT, CH₂Cl₂) → amide + DCU (peptide synthesis). Industrial: adipic acid + hexamethylenediamine → Nylon-6,6 (amide bonds).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to reflux; dry ether (diethyl ether) or THF; LiAlH₄ (anhydrous, excess 4 eq. per COOH). Mechanism: LiAlH₄ reduces COOH → aldehyde intermediate (not isolable) → primary alcohol. Cannot use NaBH₄ (too mild for carboxylic acid). Aqueous workup carefully (LiAlH₄ reacts violently with H₂O: quench with wet ether then dilute). BH₃ (milder) also reduces RCOOH → primary alcohol.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Soda-lime (NaOH + CaO) decarboxylation: dry heating 300–400°C → decarboxylation, R-COO⁻Na⁺ + CaO → R-H + CaCO₃ + Na₂CO₃. Dry distillation of calcium carboxylate salt (calcium salt + CaO, heat → alkane). Alternatively: Kolbe electrolysis (2RCOONa → R-R + 2CO₂ + 2NaOH at anode, gives symmetric alkane). Silver salt + Br₂/CCl₄ → Hunsdiecker reaction → R-Br (one carbon shorter).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ): Step 1: P (red or white) + Br₂ → PBr₃ in situ; Step 2: PBr₃ + RCOOH → acyl bromide (RCOBr) → enolisation at α-carbon → α-bromoacyl bromide → reaction with next RCOOH → α-bromo acid. Selective α-halogenation. Requires α-H. Cl₂ or Br₂ with P catalyst. Product: α-halo acid used for Gabriel, Strecker, SN2 displacement.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; base (pyridine or Et₃N, 1 eq) to neutralise HCl; anhydrous CH₂Cl₂; acyl chloride (RCOCl) + amine → amide + HCl (neutralised by base). Primary amine → monosubstituted amide (secondary amide). Secondary amine → disubstituted amide (tertiary amide). Acyl anhydride reacts similarly but slower (no HCl, gives acid + amide). DCC coupling: RT, CH₂Cl₂, for carboxylic acid + amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0–5°C (CRITICAL: must maintain 0–5°C; >5°C → diazonium decomposes, PhN₂⁺ → phenol); aqueous HCl (or HBF₄); NaNO₂. Mechanism: HNO₂ (in situ from NaNO₂ + HCl) + ArNH₂ → ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ (diazonium salt). Primary aromatic amines only (aliphatic diazonium too unstable). Maintain cold strictly. ArN₂⁺ is electrophile for coupling; or undergoes Sandmeyer, Balz-Schiemann, Gattermann reactions.
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: Slight acid catalysis (pH 4–5); aqueous-alcoholic; –H₂O (condensation). Primary amine + aldehyde/ketone → hemiaminal → imine. Identical to Schiff base formation. 2° amine gives enamine (not imine). Use molecular sieves or Dean-Stark for dehydration. Reversible (acid hydrolysis regenerates carbonyl + amine). Imines used in reductive amination (NaBH₃CN/H⁺ → amine).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Sandmeyer reaction: Step 1: CuX (CuCl, CuBr, CuCN) + ArN₂⁺ → ArX (Ar-Cl, Ar-Br, Ar-CN); RT to mild heat; aqueous or aqueous-acetone. Copper(I) acts as catalyst/reagent via single-electron mechanism. Balz-Schiemann: ArN₂⁺BF₄⁻ (from HBF₄) → heat dry → ArF + N₂ + BF₃ (for fluoride). Gattermann: Cu powder (not CuX) for Cl/Br (milder alternative to Sandmeyer).
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: Aqueous acid; heat (steam distillation conditions); H₂O. Warm/boil: ArN₂⁺ + H₂O → [Ar⁺] → ArOH + N₂. Mechanism: ArSN1-like (phenyl cation or tight ion pair). Dilute H₂SO₄ (not HCl; Cl⁻ might compete). Product: phenol. Used industrially (cumene process preferred now). Warm the diazonium salt solution gently to avoid explosive decomposition.
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: H₃PO₂ (hypophosphorous acid) + water; RT to mild heat. Mechanism: radical → Ar• + N₂ → Ar• + H (from H₃PO₂) → ArH. Alternatively: EtOH (also reductive, gives ArH). Removes amino group from aromatic ring with no substituent replacement (deamination). Useful for: install NH₂ as ortho/para director, then remove after synthesis.
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0–5°C; alkaline or slightly acidic aqueous; electrophilic aromatic substitution (coupling). ArN₂⁺ (electrophile) + Ar'OH (phenol, coupling at para position, alkaline) or Ar'NH₂ (amine, coupling at para position, neutral/acidic). pH control critical: too acidic → protonates amine coupling partner (less nucleophilic). Product: azo dye Ar-N=N-Ar'. Used in azo dyes (Congo red, methyl orange, etc.).
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to 55°C; mixed acid (conc HNO₃ + conc H₂SO₄, 1:1 v/v); nitronium ion (NO₂⁺) generated by H₂SO₄ protonating HNO₃. Mechanism: NO₂⁺ electrophile attacks benzene ring (EAS); Wheland intermediate (arenium ion); loss of H⁺ → nitrobenzene. Temperature control: >60°C gives dinitrobenzene. Mono-nitration gives nitrobenzene (meta-director for further EAS).
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; anhydrous conditions; Lewis acid catalyst (FeCl₃ for Cl₂; AlCl₃ or FeBr₃ for Br₂); halogenation EAS. Mechanism: X₂ + FeCl₃ → X⁺ (or polarised X-X) → attacks benzene ring → Wheland arenium ion → deprotonation → halobenzene + HX + regenerated Lewis acid. No catalyst needed with phenol/aniline (ring very activated). Iodination with I₂ alone is too slow → use ICl, or I₂/HNO₃, or I₂/HIO₃.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Fuming H₂SO₄ (oleum, H₂SO₄ + SO₃); 60–80°C; SO₃ is the electrophile (stronger than in conc H₂SO₄). Mechanism: SO₃ (electrophile) → attacks benzene → Wheland intermediate → loss of H⁺ → sulphonic acid. Reversible (acid hydrolysis at 150–200°C removes sulphonic acid group — useful for blocking/directing). Naphthalene sulphonation: α-product at low T, β-product at high T.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Friedel-Crafts alkylation: anhydrous conditions; AlCl₃ (or BF₃, FeCl₃) Lewis acid catalyst; RT to mild heat. R-X + AlCl₃ → R⁺AlCl₄⁻ (or polarised complex) → alkylation of benzene. Limitations: (1) carbocation rearrangements (1° RX → 2° or 3° R⁺); (2) polyalkylation (product more reactive than benzene); (3) does NOT work with deactivated rings (nitrobenzene). No rearrangement with Friedel-Crafts acylation.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Friedel-Crafts acylation: anhydrous AlCl₃ (>1 equiv, needed to complex with product ketone); dry CH₂Cl₂ or CS₂ or nitrobenzene solvent; RT to reflux. RCOCl + AlCl₃ → RCO⁺ (acylium, resonance-stabilised, no rearrangement). Acylium attacks benzene → ketone. Product (ketone) complexes with AlCl₃ → aqueous workup to liberate ketone. Deactivated rings (NO₂, COOH substituents) do not undergo FC alkylation/acylation.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: –78°C to 0°C; dry ether (Et₂O) or THF; anhydrous; HCHO (formaldehyde, gas or paraformaldehyde) added to RMgX → addition. Step 2: Aqueous workup H₃O⁺ (NH₄Cl/H₂O); RT. Product: primary alcohol with one more C than Grignard (RMgX + HCHO → R-CH₂-OH). Strictly anhydrous throughout; moisture destroys Grignard (R-MgX + H₂O → R-H + Mg(OH)X).
valid_transformations.notes: Strict anhydrous conditions required. Proton source (H₂O, ROH) destroys Grignard before reaction with substrate.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: 0°C to RT; dry Et₂O or THF; anhydrous; RCHO (aldehyde) + R'MgX → addition to carbonyl. Step 2: Aqueous workup (NH₄Cl/H₂O or dilute H₂SO₄). Product: secondary alcohol (new C-C bond formed, new stereocentre = racemic mixture). Carbonyl carbon hybridisation changes sp²→sp³. Grignard is organometallic base as well as nucleophile: avoid acidic H (OH, NH, SH, terminal alkyne).
valid_transformations.notes: Strict anhydrous conditions required. Proton source (H₂O, ROH) destroys Grignard before reaction with substrate.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: 0°C to RT; dry Et₂O or THF; anhydrous; R₂CO (ketone) + R''MgX → addition. Step 2: Aqueous workup. Product: tertiary alcohol (three different or same R groups). Steric hindrance of ketone can slow reaction (especially with aryl Grignard + hindered ketone). Use THF (higher bp, better solvation). Product: R₂C(OH)-R'' with two stereocentres possible.
valid_transformations.notes: Strict anhydrous conditions required. Proton source (H₂O, ROH) destroys Grignard before reaction with substrate.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: 0°C to RT; dry Et₂O or THF; dry CO₂ gas (passed through Grignard solution or solid dry ice added) + RMgX → addition → MgX-carboxylate. Step 2: Aqueous workup (H₃O⁺). Product: RCOOH (one carbon more than Grignard). Mechanism: nucleophilic addition of R⁻ to electrophilic C of CO₂. Double addition prevented (carboxylate is much less reactive than CO₂ toward RMgX).
valid_transformations.notes: Strict anhydrous conditions required. Proton source (H₂O, ROH) destroys Grignard before reaction with substrate.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux; aqueous acidic (dil H₂SO₄, H₃O⁺) or aqueous basic (NaOH/H₂O) conditions. Mechanism (acid hydrolysis): R-CN + H₂O/H⁺ → R-CO-NH₂ (amide intermediate) → R-COOH + NH₄⁺. Basic: R-CN + NaOH → R-COO⁻Na⁺ + NH₃ → acid on workup. Nitrile hydrolysis: acid > primary amide > carboxylic acid (2 additions of H₂O). Can stop at amide stage with controlled conditions.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Anhydrous conditions for LiAlH₄; dry ether; 0°C to reflux; LiAlH₄ (excess, 2 eq.) → reduces CN to CH₂-NH₂. Aqueous workup (careful). Alternative: H₂/Ni (Raney Ni, 50–100 psi H₂, EtOH, RT–50°C). Na + EtOH (partial reduction possible). Product: primary amine with one more C than nitrile (chain length same as original nitrile but plus NH₂). Used in Gabriel synthesis product liberation.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; aqueous acid (dilute H₂SO₄ or HCl, pH 2–4) or aqueous base (NaOH). Acid opening: H⁺ protonates O → ring strain drives SN1-like opening at more substituted C (Markovnikov) → H₂O attacks from back → anti-diol (trans). Base opening: HO⁻ attacks at less hindered C (SN2, anti addition) → anti-diol. Either way: anti addition of two OH groups across former double bond.
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemical outcome critical: syn addition (mCPBA), then ring-opening gives anti-addition overall. Track face selectivity carefully.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; anhydrous (or slightly acidic for HX); HX (HCl, HBr, HI). Acid opens epoxide at more substituted C (SN1-like via oxocarbenium) → halide attacks → anti-addition. Trans diaxial opening preferred for cyclohexene epoxides. Product: β-halohydrin (trans if from symmetrical alkene). HBr/HCl: X attacks at more substituted C under acidic conditions.
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemical outcome critical: syn addition (mCPBA), then ring-opening gives anti-addition overall. Track face selectivity carefully.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; neat amine or amine in EtOH or THF; primary or secondary amine (RNH₂ or R₂NH) opens epoxide. Without acid catalyst: amine (better nucleophile than H₂O) attacks at less hindered C (SN2, anti addition) → β-amino alcohol. With acid: more substituted C attacked (SN1-like). Product: trans-β-amino alcohol. Used in synthesis of amino alcohols for asymmetric synthesis.
valid_transformations.notes: Stereochemical outcome critical: syn addition (mCPBA), then ring-opening gives anti-addition overall. Track face selectivity carefully.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to reflux; dry ether or THF; LiAlH₄ (excess, anhydrous). Mechanism: LiAlH₄ delivers H⁻ twice to amide C=O → carbinolamine → further reduction → amine. Net: C=O reduced to CH₂ (no carbon loss). Gives 1° amine RCH₂NH₂ (one more CH₂ than amide carbonyl C). Careful aqueous workup. NaBH₄ does NOT reduce amides.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to reflux; dry ether or THF; LiAlH₄ (excess). N-substituted amide reduced to N-substituted amine. Same mechanism: C=O → CH₂. Product is secondary amine. Aqueous workup (Zemplén: add wet ether dropwise, then water, then dilute NaOH → filter Mg(OH)₂). Reaction is exothermic — add LiAlH₄ cautiously.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to reflux; dry ether or THF; LiAlH₄. N,N-disubstituted amide → tertiary amine. C=O reduced to CH₂. Product is tertiary amine with same C count as original amide carbon backbone. Same mechanism as for 1° and 2° amides.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0°C to reflux; dry ether or THF; LiAlH₄ (excess). Ring C=O reduced to CH₂ → cyclic amine (N remains in ring). e.g., pyrrolidinone → pyrrolidine; caprolactam → hexamethyleneimine. Same mechanism. Product ring size same as lactam.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Hofmann rearrangement (Hofmann degradation): aqueous NaOH; Br₂; RT to mild heat. Mechanism: (1) Br₂ + NaOH → NaOBr (hypobromate); (2) amide N-H deprotonated → N-bromo amide → base removes 2nd N-H → N-bromo amide anion → rearrangement (alkyl migrates from C to N with loss of N₂ → isocyanate R-N=C=O) → H₂O hydrolysis of isocyanate → carbamic acid → decarboxylation → RNH₂. Net: amide loses one carbon.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reflux in aqueous ethanol or aqueous HCl; Sn/HCl (tin in conc HCl) or Fe/HCl or Zn/HCl or H₂/Pd. Mechanism: 6e⁻ reduction; Sn or Fe acts as electron source in acid. Industrial: H₂/catalyst (Cu-Cr oxide or Ni, 200°C). Lab: Sn/conc HCl → amine-SnCl₂ complex → basify (NaOH) → free amine. Also: catalytic hydrogenation (H₂, Pd/C, RT, 1 atm).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: RT; aqueous ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl, weakly acidic/neutral pH); Zn dust. Mechanism: 4e⁻ reduction; controlled by pH — neutral conditions stop at hydroxylamine. More basic → further reduction to amine. Zn/NH₄Cl: neutral reducing conditions. Product: N-arylhydroxylamine. Used for Bamberger rearrangement (→ 4-aminophenol with H₂SO₄).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 1 equiv Zn; aqueous NaOH (1 mol, mildly basic); RT. Bimolecular reductive coupling: ArNO₂ reduced to nitrosobenzene (ArNO, 2e⁻) → condensation with ArNHOH → azobenzene via hydrazone-like TS. Basic conditions. Product is trans-azobenzene (thermodynamic). cis-azobenzene from photoisomerisation of trans.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: 2 equiv Zn (or excess) or LiAlH₄; aqueous NaOH (strongly basic); reflux. 4e⁻ reduction: each ArNO₂ → ArNH•, then bimolecular coupling → ArNH-NHAr (hydrazobenzene). Acid-catalysed rearrangement of hydrazobenzene → benzidine (4,4'-diaminobiphenyl). LiAlH₄ in dry ether also gives hydrazobenzene.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: 3 equiv Zn (or slight excess) or Na₂AsO₂; aqueous NaOH; mild conditions. 2e⁻ reduction per nitro group → nitrosobenzene; nitroso + hydroxylamine (from partial reduction) → azoxy. Or: controlled reduction of azobenzene with mCPBA gives azoxybenzene. Azoxybenzene is intermediate between azobenzene and nitrosobenzene in the reduction series.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.to: selective reduction of less electron-deficient NO2 to NH2
valid_transformations.conditions: RT to mild heat; aqueous ethanol; (NH₄)₂S (ammonium sulphide) or NH₄SH (ammonium hydrosulphide); 1 equiv. Selective reduction: the NO₂ group that is LEAST activated toward nucleophilic attack (least electron-poor, less flanked by EWG) is selectively reduced. Chemoselective: reduces NO₂ adjacent to EDG over NO₂ adjacent to EWG. Staudinger: PPh₃ also reduces 1 NO₂ selectively in polynitro compounds.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

reagents: H2/Pt or H2/Pd or H2/Ni or LAH
valid_transformations.conditions: H₂/Pt or H₂/Pd (1–3 atm, RT to 50°C, EtOH) or LiAlH₄ (dry ether, 0°C to reflux). H₂ with Raney Ni (50 psi, 50°C, NH₃ added to suppress secondary amine formation by blocking imine intermediate). LiAlH₄ route: more reliable, anhydrous. Product: primary amine, one more CH₂ than original nitrile. With Raney Ni + NH₃: minimise over-reduction to secondary amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: H₂/Pt (1 atm, RT to 50°C, EtOH or AcOH) or LiAlH₄ (dry ether). Isocyanide is reduced to secondary methylamine: R-NC + 2[H₂] → R-NH-CH₃. The C of isocyanide (originally NC:) picks up 2H atoms → methyl group. Mechanism: H₂ adds to C≡N triple bond. Product is N-methyl secondary amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reductive amination: Step 1 (imine formation): pH 4–5, RT or mild heat, NH₄OAc or NH₃/EtOH, –H₂O. Step 2 (reduction of imine): H₂/Pd (RT, 1 atm, EtOH) or NaBH₃CN (RT, MeOH, pH 6–7). NaBH₃CN is selective: reduces iminium (not carbonyls, unlike NaBH₄). Product: primary amine from aldehyde + NH₃; secondary amine from ketone + NH₃.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Reductive amination: Step 1 (imine): pH 4–5, RT, RNH₂ (primary amine) + RCHO/R₂CO, –H₂O. Step 2: NaBH₃CN (pH 6, MeOH) or H₂/Pd (1 atm, EtOH). Product: secondary amine (one new N-C bond). Catalytic hydrogenation at RT; NaBH₃CN is more selective at RT. Iminium ion (protonated imine) is the actual electrophile reduced by NaBH₃CN.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: Dean-Stark, reflux toluene or benzene; 2° amine (R₂NH) + R₃CO/R₃CHO → enamine (R₃NH + ketone → iminium → deprotonation at α-C → enamine). Step 2: reduce enamine (H₂/Pd or NaBH₃CN, pH 6). Product: tertiary amine. Enamines are also useful as nucleophilic enol equivalents (alkylation then hydrolysis → α-substituted ketone).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.to: mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary ammonium salt
valid_transformations.conditions: Heat; SN2 at primary alkyl halide; sealed tube or pressure vessel; excess R-X. Each successive alkylation requires R-X and heat. Control: (1) excess NH₃ favours primary; (2) excess R-X drives quaternary. Separation difficult — use Gabriel synthesis for pure primary amine. Hoffmann exhaustive methylation (CH₃I excess → quaternary ammonium salt → Ag₂O/H₂O → base → Hofmann elimination).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'II'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 450°C; Al₂O₃ catalyst; gas phase; high temperature. Mechanism: dehydration of alcohol → alkene (or ether) → then amine formation via Leuckart mechanism or direct substitution. Al₂O₃ catalyses both dehydration and amine synthesis. Preferentially gives tertiary amine (thermodynamic product at high T). Industrial route to triethylamine from ethanol + NH₃.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Ritter reaction: conc H₂SO₄ (or other strong acid) + HCN (or nitrile R'CN); RT to mild heat. Mechanism: acid protonates alcohol → carbocation → HCN (nucleophile, via N) attacks → nitrilium ion (R-C≡N-H⁺ or R-N⁺=C:) → H₂O addition → amide → hydrolysis → amine. 3° alcohols react best (most stable carbocation). Product is N-monosubstituted amide first, then hydrolysis gives primary amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Carbocation intermediate: check for rearrangement (1,2-H or 1,2-alkyl shift) if a more stable cation is accessible.

valid_transformations.conditions: Mannich reaction: aqueous EtOH or MeOH; slight acidity (pH 4–5, AcOH); RT to mild heat (50°C). Three components: ketone (with α-H) + HCHO + NH₃ (or primary/secondary amine). Mechanism: HCHO + NH₃ → iminium (H₂C=NH₂⁺) → enol attacks iminium → Mannich base (β-amino carbonyl). Product: β-aminoketone. Quaternary if 2° amine used (Mannich base with no N-H).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Schmidt reaction: conc H₂SO₄; HN₃ (hydrazoic acid, generated in situ from NaN₃ + H₂SO₄); 0°C to RT. Mechanism: RCOOH protonated → acylium (RCO⁺) → HN₃ attacks → loss of N₂ → isocyanate (R-N=C=O) → H₂O → carbamic acid → CO₂ + RNH₂. One fewer C than original acid. Also works for ketones → amide (ring expansion) and for alcohols → nitrilium.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Curtius rearrangement: Step 1 (acyl azide formation): RT; Et₂O or THF; NaN₃ + RCOCl → RCON₃ + NaCl. Step 2 (rearrangement): gentle heat (50–80°C) → RCON₃ loses N₂ → isocyanate R-N=C=O. Step 3: H₂O → carbamic acid → CO₂ + RNH₂. Or trap isocyanate with ROH → urethane (carbamate). One C fewer than acid chloride. Milder than Schmidt.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Lossen rearrangement: Step 1: Ac₂O (acetic anhydride) + hydroxamic acid RCONHOH → O-acylated hydroxamic acid RCONHOCOCH₃; Step 2: base (OH⁻, heat) → loss of AcO⁻ → isocyanate R-N=C=O → H₂O → RNH₂ + CO₂. Similar to Hofmann and Curtius. Isocyanate intermediate common to all. Product: primary amine one C shorter.
valid_transformations.notes: Rearrangement step: product carbon skeleton differs from substrate. Always verify whether migration occurs before assigning product structure.

reagents: KOH, then RX, then OH-/H2O, then H+
valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: KOH (or K₂CO₃)/EtOH; phthalimide + KOH → potassium phthalimide (N-K salt). Step 2: DMF or DMSO; R-X (primary only, SN2) + K-phthalimide → N-alkylphthalimide. Step 3: NaOH (aq., reflux) or NH₂NH₂ (hydrazinolysis, EtOH reflux) → primary amine RNH₂ + phthalate. Hydrazinolysis preferred (milder, no saponification of ester). Gives pure primary amine (no over-alkylation).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0–5°C (strict temperature control); aqueous HCl (2 equiv); NaNO₂ (1 equiv). Same as amine→diazonium entry. HNO₂ (in situ) + ArNH₂ → ArN₂⁺. ArN₂⁺BF₄⁻ (from HBF₄) is isolable solid (Balz-Schiemann precursor). Keep cold at all times during preparation and use.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: 0–5°C; alkaline aqueous (NaOH or Na₂CO₃, pH 9–10); coupling at para position of β-naphthol. Electrophilic aromatic substitution: ArN₂⁺ (electrophile) + β-naphthol (highly activated ring, coupling at C-1, para to OH) → azo dye. Alkaline pH keeps naphthol as phenoxide (more nucleophilic). Acidic → protonates coupling partner → slower. Product: intensely coloured orange-red azo compound.
valid_transformations.notes: Temperature critical: 0–5°C for stable arenediazonium. Aliphatic diazonium decomposes immediately. Coupling requires alkaline medium.

valid_transformations.conditions: Benzidine rearrangement: conc HCl (or dilute H₂SO₄); heat (60–80°C); acid-catalysed [3,3]-sigmatropic-like or radical cation mechanism. Protonation of both N atoms → dication → reorganisation → 4,4'-diaminobiphenyl (major, ~70%) + 2,4'-diaminobiphenyl (semidine, minor). Acid concentration controls product ratio. Benzidine is a carcinogen; IUPAC: 4,4'-diaminobiphenyl.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: Hofmann-Martius rearrangement: dry heat 200°C (neat or high-boiling solvent); no acid needed (salt itself rearranges on heating). Mechanism: N-alkyl cleaves → free alkyl cation (or tight ion pair) → electrophilic alkylation of ring at ortho (kinetic) or para (thermodynamic) position. Product: o- and p-alkylanilines. Used to interconvert N-alkyl and C-alkyl anilines.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.to: para-nitroso primary amine (NO migrates N to ring para)
valid_transformations.conditions: Fischer-Hepp rearrangement: dilute HCl (aqueous); RT or mild heat; N-nitroso compound (R-N(NO)-Ph or Ar). Mechanism: N-nitroso protonated → nitrosyl cation (NO⁺) migrates intramolecularly to para position of ring → para-nitroso aniline derivative. Requires secondary aromatic amine with at least one N-H. Regioselective para.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Oxidation under acidic or neutral conditions: KMnO₄ (acidic, hot, excess), K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄, or H₂O₂ (H₂O₂/AcOH). PhNH₂ → p-benzoquinone (6e⁻ oxidation per molecule) via aniline radical cation → quinone imine → hydrolysis → quinone. Acidic conditions favour quinone; basic conditions may give azobenzene-type products instead.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Caro's acid (H₂SO₅, peroxomonosulphuric acid): direct N-oxidation. RT to mild heat; aqueous. Caro's acid is a powerful electrophilic oxygen source: PhNH₂ → PhNHOH → PhNO₂ (sequential N-oxidation). Peracids (mCPBA) can also directly oxidise aromatic amines to nitro in some cases. Not commonly used but mechanistically interesting.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: KMnO₄ (acidic, hot, conc); over-oxidation: R-CH₂-NH₂ → R-CH=NH (aldiimine) → R-CHO (hydrolysis) → R-COOH (further oxidation). Note: KMnO₄ with primary amines is vigorous and gives complex mixtures; the product depends on conditions. Hot acidic KMnO₄ tends to give carboxylic acid. Mild oxidation (CuO, 300°C) gives nitrile.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: KMnO₄ (neutral or mildly basic, aqueous); RT to mild heat. Mechanism: oxidation of NH₂ → NHOH → NO₂ (successive 2e⁻ oxidations). 3° primary amine → 3° nitro compound (no alpha H for elimination side reactions). KMnO₄ less prone to over-oxidation for these substrates.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.to: nitroso compound R2N-N=O or hydroxylamine derivative
valid_transformations.conditions: KMnO₄ (aqueous, mild to moderate conditions); RT. Secondary amines oxidised to N-nitrosoamines (R₂N-NO) or N,N-disubstituted hydroxylamines depending on conditions. Nitrosoamines are carcinogenic. Alternative: mCPBA gives N-oxide (R₂N→O) from tertiary amines; secondary amines → more complex.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

reagents: mCPBA or H2O2 or O3 or Ag2O
valid_transformations.conditions: mCPBA (or H₂O₂ 30%, or m-CPBA in CH₂Cl₂); RT; CH₂Cl₂ or EtOH solvent. Nucleophilic addition of peroxyacid O to lone pair of N: R₃N + peracid → R₃N⁺-O⁻ + carboxylate. Amine oxide (N-oxide): stable, zwitterionic, water-soluble. Cope elimination: heat N-oxide → alkene + hydroxylamine (syn elimination, mild, without base). Used in Cope elimination for E-selective alkene synthesis.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: KMnO₄ (aqueous) does NOT oxidise tertiary amines (no N-H bond, no α-H for oxidation pathway). Tertiary amines resist oxidation by KMnO₄. Contrast: 1° amines → aldehyde → acid; 2° amines → nitroso; 3° amines → no reaction with KMnO₄ (different from mCPBA which gives N-oxide).
valid_transformations.notes: This transformation is deliberately marked as a failed/blocked reaction — a common JEE trap where students predict a product when none forms.

valid_transformations.conditions: Hofmann exhaustive test: RT; aqueous or alcoholic; diethyl oxalate (EtOOC-COOEt) + 1° amine → N,N'-disubstituted oxalamide (RHN-CO-CO-NHR, insoluble, precipitate). Distinguishes from 2° amine (gives N,N-disubstituted oxalamide, liquid). 3° amine → no reaction (no N-H). Precipitate characteristic of 1° aliphatic amine.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Hofmann test: RT; diethyl oxalate + 2° amine → N,N-disubstituted oxalamide (R₂N-CO-CO-NR₂ or R₂N-CO-CO-NR₂); liquid (oily) because more substituted → less intermolecular H-bonding. Distinguish from 1° amine (solid precipitate) and 3° amine (no reaction). Useful for classification of unknown amines.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.note: Intermediate is sodium phenoxide; must acidify. Extreme conditions because ArCl normally unreactive toward SNAr.
valid_transformations.conditions: Dow's process: 623K (350°C), 300 atm, concentrated NaOH (steam); then acid workup (H⁺). Mechanism: benzyne (aryne) intermediate (E2-like elimination of HCl → aryne → HO⁻ addition). High temperature and pressure needed due to poor leaving-group ability of Cl on aromatic ring. Industrial scale: chlorobenzene + NaOH(steam) → sodium phenoxide → H⁺ → phenol. No Lewis acid (aryl halides unreactive in EAS conditions).
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Fenton generates OH radical which hydroxylates benzene.
valid_transformations.conditions: Fenton's reagent: FeSO₄ + H₂O₂; RT; aqueous acidic (H₂SO₄). Generates HO• (hydroxyl radical): Fe²⁺ + H₂O₂ → Fe³⁺ + HO• + HO⁻. HO• adds to benzene → cyclohexadienyl radical → oxidation → phenol. Also: photochemical (UV + H₂O₂), ozone/water, or biological hydroxylation (cytochrome P450). Lab preparation: impractical; industrial: cumene process preferred.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Diazonium ion undergoes ArSN1 (NOT SN2) — phenyl cation intermediate.
valid_transformations.conditions: Warm aqueous acid (dilute H₂SO₄ or HCl, 60–80°C); heat ArN₂⁺ in dilute H₂SO₄ → N₂ evolution → phenol. Mechanism: ArSN1 via phenyl cation (or tight ion pair) → H₂O attacks → phenol + N₂. Do NOT use concentrated acid (risk of explosive N₂ evolution). Use dilute H₂SO₄ (not HCl — Cl⁻ competes). Temperature: warm gently (steam bath), do not boil vigorously.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Ar migrates preferentially (Ar > R > H) in 1,2-shift of protonated CHP. Co-product acetone is often forgotten by students.
valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: RT, air/O₂, radical initiator (or sunlight, or simply air at industrial scale) → cumene hydroperoxide (Ph-C(CH₃)₂-OOH); 80–120°C, autoxidation. Step 2: Dilute H₂SO₄ (dil, 5–10%), RT to 60°C; acid-catalysed cleavage of O-O bond → phenol + acetone. Industrial: cumene (isopropylbenzene) + O₂ → CUMHP → H₂SO₄ → phenol + acetone. Both products valuable.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Ph₂CH-OOH → protonation → Ph migrates → Ph-CH(OPh⁺) → H₂O → PhCHO + PhOH
valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: RT to 80°C; O₂ (air), radical initiator → diphenylmethyl hydroperoxide (Ph₂CH-OOH). Step 2: Dilute H₂SO₄; acid-catalysed O-O homolysis or heterolysis → Ph₂C=O (benzophenone, initially) or PhCHO + PhOH depending on mechanism. Oxidative cleavage at the benzylic C-H position (activated by 2 phenyl groups). Contrast with cumene which gives ketone + phenol cleanly.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.from: 4-methoxyphenyl 4-nitrophenyl methane (diarylmethane with OMe and NO₂ groups)
valid_transformations.note: Electron-rich (OMe) aryl ring migrates preferentially over electron-poor (NO₂) ring. Selective migration based on electron density.
valid_transformations.conditions: O₂ (air), radical initiator or autoxidation; 80–120°C; then acid workup (dil H₂SO₄). Unsymmetrical diarylmethane: electron-rich p-OMe aryl stabilises radical/cation intermediate → O₂ attack → hydroperoxide → cleavage → p-methoxyphenol + p-nitrobenzaldehyde. Migration: electron-rich Ar (OMe) stays as phenol; electron-poor Ar (NO₂) becomes aldehyde.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['III', 'IV'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.note: Migration order: -COO⁻/ester > R > Ar. Counter to carbocation chemistry where Ar migrates best. 1,2-shift on protonated dienone.
valid_transformations.conditions: Dienone-Phenol rearrangement: H⁺ (conc H₂SO₄ or HCl), heat (Δ). Mechanism: protonation of C=O → allylic cation at C-4 → 1,2-shift of better migrating group (COOEt > Ph > Me) → dienyl cation → loss of H⁺ → aromatic phenol. Driving force: aromatisation. Acid catalyst essential. Migration aptitude: COOEt > Ph > Me.
valid_transformations.notes: Rearrangement step: product carbon skeleton differs from substrate. Always verify whether migration occurs before assigning product structure.

valid_transformations.to: o-hydroxy aryl ketone or p-hydroxy aryl ketone (Fries rearrangement)
valid_transformations.note: Acyl migrates from O to ring (ortho or para). Low T → para; high T → ortho. Gives both OH and COR on ring.
valid_transformations.conditions: Fries rearrangement: AlCl₃ (Lewis acid, >1 equiv); anhydrous; heat (Δ, 100–200°C); CS₂, PhNO₂ or nitrobenzene solvent; or neat. Low T (room to 100°C) → ortho product (thermodynamic control of intramolecular delivery). High T (>150°C) → para product. Photo-Fries (UV, RT) → predominantly ortho. AlCl₃ cleaves ester O-CO → acylium → intramolecular FC acylation of phenol ring.
valid_transformations.notes: Rearrangement step: product carbon skeleton differs from substrate. Always verify whether migration occurs before assigning product structure.

valid_transformations.note: Pericyclic [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement. Allyl migrates to ortho with inversion of allyl terminus (γ-C bonds to ring).
valid_transformations.conditions: Thermal Claisen rearrangement: heat (Δ, 200–250°C); no catalyst required; neat or high-boiling solvent (diethylaniline). Mechanism: [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement (pericyclic, chair-like TS); allyl group migrates from O to C-2 (ortho) with inversion at γ-carbon (γ,γ'-connectivity). If ortho blocked → further Cope → para product (Claisen-Cope). Product: 2-allylphenol (ortho). Stereospecific (E-allyl ether → Z-allylic C at product).
valid_transformations.notes: Rearrangement step: product carbon skeleton differs from substrate. Always verify whether migration occurs before assigning product structure.

valid_transformations.note: Acid catalysis → Novolac (linear, thermoplastic). Further heating with excess HCHO → Bakelite (thermoset, crosslinked network).
valid_transformations.conditions: Novolac: acid catalyst (conc H₂SO₄ or HCl, oxalic acid); phenol:HCHO > 1:1; 50–100°C → linear ortho/para-linked phenol-formaldehyde resin. Bakelite: Novolac + excess HCHO, base catalyst (NaOH, hexamethylenetetramine); heat + pressure (150–175°C, 10–15 atm) → 3D crosslinked thermosetting network. Once cured → irreversible (cannot re-melt). Thermoset vs thermoplastic distinction.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.note: Phenol reacts with Na and NaOH but NOT Na₂CO₃ (pKa ~10, not acidic enough for carbonate).
valid_transformations.conditions: Na: RT; dry phenol + Na metal → Na-phenoxide + ½H₂ (vigorous, exothermic). NaOH: aqueous; phenol is stronger acid than H₂O (pKa 10) → reacts with NaOH (aq) completely. NaHCO₃: phenol does NOT react (pKa 10 < pKa CO₂/H₂O ~ 6.4, so phenol too weak to displace bicarbonate). Na₂CO₃: phenol reacts. PhOH + NaOH → PhO⁻Na⁺ + H₂O. Sodium phenoxide used for Williamson ether synthesis and Kolbe-Schmitt.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: O-Methylation: CH₂N₂ (diazomethane): RT; anhydrous ether; very fast, quantitative; O-selective (not C-methylation). Me₂SO₄ (dimethyl sulfate): PhO⁻Na⁺ + Me₂SO₄ → PhOMe + MeSO₄⁻Na⁺; RT to mild heat; aqueous base; SN2. Phase transfer catalysis useful for Me₂SO₄. CH₂N₂ preferred in lab (no aqueous needed, no base). Reactivity PhOH with CH₂N₂: RCOOH > PhOH > ROH.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.conditions: O-Acylation: acyl chloride RCOCl + phenol → PhOCOR + HCl; base (pyridine or Et₃N) to neutralise HCl; RT; anhydrous CH₂Cl₂. Alternatively: acyl anhydride (RCO)₂O + phenol (no base needed if mild, or NaOH for sodium phenoxide → acylation). C-acylation (Fries) requires AlCl₃ + heat. O-acylation favoured at RT; C-acylation at high T with Lewis acid.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

reagents: Br₂/H₂O (aqueous, NO Lewis acid catalyst needed)
valid_transformations.note: Ring is so activated by -OH that tribromination occurs spontaneously in water. White precipitate used for identification.
valid_transformations.conditions: Aqueous bromine (Br₂/H₂O); RT; no Lewis acid catalyst needed. Phenol ring is highly activated by OH (strong EDG, ortho/para director) → three electrophilic Br attacks spontaneously in aqueous solution. OH deprotonated (as phenoxide) even more activated. Product: 2,4,6-tribromophenol precipitates (white solid, low solubility). Test for phenol (immediate white precipitate with Br₂ water). Contrast: 1 equiv Br₂/non-polar solvent (CCl₄) → monobromination.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'II'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.note: Non-polar solvent prevents ionisation of Br₂; mono-para substitution only. Contrasts with aqueous tribromination.
valid_transformations.conditions: Non-polar solvent (CS₂ or CCl₄); RT; Br₂ (1 equiv); no Lewis acid. In non-polar solvent, phenol is less activated than in water (OH not partially ionised) → selective mono para-bromination. Electrophile: Br₂ (polarised by ring π-electrons). Para preferred over ortho (steric). In aqueous: tribromination. In CS₂/CCl₄: mono-para product. Temperature: room temperature.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Dilute HNO₃ (20%); RT or 0°C; aqueous. Electrophile: NO₂⁺ (nitronium, from dilute HNO₃ equilibrium). Phenol activated → easy nitration under mild conditions (unlike benzene which needs mixed acid). Products: o-nitrophenol (volatile, intramolecular H-bond, steam-distillable) and p-nitrophenol (inter-H-bond, high mp, not steam-distillable) in ~1:1 ratio. Separation by steam distillation (ortho distils, para stays).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'II'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Step 1: conc H₂SO₄ + phenol → sulphonation at ortho/para (blocks ring, activates para position); Step 2: conc HNO₃/H₂SO₄ → nitration replaces sulphonic acid groups and direct nitration → picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol). Alternative: conc HNO₃ alone (fuming) with phenol, careful temperature control. Picric acid: explosive when dry; keep moist. Strong acid (pKa 0.4).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

reagents: KMnO₄ OR Na₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ OR conc HNO₃
valid_transformations.conditions: Na₂Cr₂O₇/dil H₂SO₄ (aqueous, mild oxidation); RT to mild heat. Alternatively: KMnO₄ (dilute, acidic); FeCl₃/O₂; conc HNO₃/H₂SO₄. Mechanism: 4e⁻ oxidation of phenol → p-benzoquinone (yellow solid). Also: 2,4-dinitrophenol + Na₂Cr₂O₇ → 2,4-dinitrophenol (ring deactivated, harder). Quinone/hydroquinone redox pair (reversible 2e⁻ couple, E° = +0.70 V).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Industrial: V₂O₅ catalyst; 400–450°C; O₂ (air); gas phase. Phenol vapour + O₂ → ring-opened oxidation → maleic anhydride (C₄H₂O₃). Also: benzene → maleic anhydride via V₂O₅/O₂/400°C. Side products: CO₂, H₂O. High temperature, high oxygen. Catalyst: vanadium pentoxide on support (Al₂O₃ or SiO₂). Industrial scale only.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Zn dust + heat (Δ, 300°C); dry conditions; reduction. Mechanism: Zn reduces C-OH → C-H (reductive deoxygenation). Also: H₂/catalyst (Pd/C, 200°C, high pressure → partial reduction to cyclohexanol, not benzene). Zn/Δ gives benzene directly from phenol (C-O bond broken, H supplied by Zn + moisture or from phenol itself). Occasionally used in synthesis to remove phenolic OH after it has served as directing group.
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Persulphate ion acts as electrophilic oxygen donor via sulphate ester intermediate. Hydroxylates ortho to existing OH.
valid_transformations.conditions: Elbs persulphate oxidation: K₂S₂O₈ (potassium persulphate); alkaline KOH (aq); 60–80°C. Mechanism: PhO⁻ + S₂O₈²⁻ → phenyl persulphate ester → rearrangement → para-hydroxyphenyl sulphate → base hydrolysis → hydroquinone (para-diphenol). Boyland-Sims (acid conditions): gives ortho sulphate → catechol (1,2-diphenol). Note: Elbs → para-product (hydroquinone); Boyland-Sims → ortho-product (catechol).
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: PCl₃, SOCl₂, HX, Lucas reagent (HCl/ZnCl₂) do NOT work on phenol — major difference from aliphatic alcohols.
valid_transformations.conditions: PCl₅ (phosphorus pentachloride); RT to mild heat; anhydrous; slow reaction. PhOH + PCl₅ → PhCl + POCl₃ + HCl. Unlike aliphatic alcohols (which react faster with PCl₅), phenol reacts slowly because C-O bond has partial double bond character (lone pair donation from O to ring). Product: chlorobenzene (poor yield). Alternative: ArN₂⁺ + HCl/Cu → ArCl via Sandmeyer (better for aryl chloride synthesis).
valid_transformations.notes: EAS: product regiochemistry determined by existing substituent(s). Check for conflicting or cooperating directors before assigning major product.

valid_transformations.note: Colorless pH<8.3; pink 8.3-10; colorless again >10 (excess NaOH). Both phenol and β-naphthol pass this test; 2-naphthol blocked sterically fails.
valid_transformations.conditions: Phthalein dye synthesis: conc H₂SO₄ (catalyst); phthalic anhydride + 2 phenol; Δ (150–200°C), melt or neat; Friedel-Crafts-like condensation. Product: phenolphthalein (colourless below pH 8.3, pink/red above pH 8.3 as lactone opens). Also: cresol + phthalic anhydride → cresolphthalein. Industrial preparation uses ZnCl₂ as Lewis acid catalyst.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I', 'III'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.conditions: Dry Ag₂O (silver oxide): RT; SN2 on primary or secondary R-X; dry solvent (Et₂O or acetone). Ag₂O acts as base (accepts X⁻ as AgX precipitate) and O-nucleophile source. 2 R-X + Ag₂O → R-O-R + 2 AgX↓. Mild, anhydrous. Good for simple symmetrical ethers from 1° alkyl halides. Compare: Williamson (alkoxide + R-X) for unsymmetrical ethers.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

reagents: Me₂SO₄ (dimethyl sulfate, good leaving group, SN2) OR CH₂N₂ (diazomethane)
valid_transformations.conditions: CH₂N₂ (diazomethane): RT; anhydrous ether solvent; near-instantaneous O-methylation with no workup needed. Reactivity: RCOOH >> PhOH > ROH. Me₂SO₄ (dimethyl sulphate): RONa + Me₂SO₄ → ROCH₃ + MeOSO₃Na; RT to mild heat; aqueous base (NaOH); SN2. Me₂SO₄ is toxic and volatile — handle in fume hood. CH₂N₂ safer for small scale (but explosive in high concentration).
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

valid_transformations.note: Works only for 1° alcohols. T > 170°C gives alkene (dehydration) instead. 2° and 3° alcohols give alkene even at lower T.
valid_transformations.conditions: Conc H₂SO₄; 110–140°C (110–170°C); SN2 bimolecular dehydration. Mechanism: H⁺ protonates OH → oxonium → SN2 attack by 2nd ROH molecule → ether + H₂O. Requires 1° or 2° alcohol (3° → alkene). Temperature critical: 110–140°C → ether; >170°C → alkene. Also: Al₂O₃/250°C → ether; Williamson with Na gives unsymmetrical ether.
valid_transformations.notes: Archetype ['I'] transformation. Verify conditions carefully; the reagent identity determines mechanism and hence product regiochemistry/stereochemistry.

reagents: SN2 (best with MeI or primary R'X)
valid_transformations.note: 3° R'X gives E2 elimination instead. PhO⁻ (weaker nucleophile than RO⁻) works with methyl and 1° halides but fails with 3°. Cannot make ArOR' where R' is tertiary.
valid_transformations.conditions: Williamson synthesis: RT to gentle reflux; dry aprotic solvent (DMF, DMSO, dry Et₂O or THF); SN2. Alkoxide (RO⁻Na⁺) prepared from ROH + Na metal (0°C to RT, anhydrous). MUST use primary R'-X (secondary → E2 competes; tertiary → only E2). Best: methyl, allyl, benzyl halides. Dry conditions critical (alkoxide + H₂O → ROH + OH⁻). Inversion at R'-C (SN2). For unsymmetrical ethers: use bulkier group as alkoxide, less hindered group as halide.
